Summary: The 2WikiMultihopQA original paper by Ho et al. (2020) presents a multi-hop QA dataset that enforces reasoning over structured and unstructured contexts with explicit reasoning paths and evidence annotations. The dataset includes three splits: train, validation, and test, with 113,284, 12,981, and 12,995 examples respectively. The dataset contains multi-hop question-answer pairs with supporting evidence chains drawn from Wikipedia. The evaluation metrics include span-level EM/F1, supporting fact F1/EM, and joint F1. The latest results from the GitHub repository show that on October 29, 2021, the NA-Reviewer model achieved an answer EM of 76.73, answer F1 of 81.91, supporting fact EM of 89.61, supporting fact F1 of 94.31, evidence EM of 53.66, evidence F1 of 70.83, joint EM of 52.75, and joint F1 of 65.23.
